analysis.title: "If Oil Isn't The Solve, This Gets More Complicated", Goldman One-Delta Desk Warns Energy/Rates Beta Is Breaking Down
key_insights: Equities held up on Sep 30 on AI capex support and TSMC US expansion chatter, but Privorotsky called it "one of the more disturbing cross asset days of this episode": credit widened and rates kept selling off even as oil fell.
The energy/rates beta appears to be breaking down. Lower oil is no longer relieving rates. Privorotsky: "if oil isn't the solve this gets more complicated."

Real rates are described as very high. Candidate explanations are a carry unwind as yen appreciation cuts global balance-sheet capacity, and rates volatility so extreme that the Street is unwilling or unable to intermediate.
Privorotsky offers a structural explanation: elevated real yields may be the clearing price for fiscally dominant economies that need private capital to fund large sovereign borrowing.

Higher risk-free real yields raise the hurdle rate for equities. Private savings may have to be pulled from risky assets toward government debt, which reverses the years-long push of investors out the risk curve.

Oil: "more talk, more back and forth, still no concrete solution." Hormuz flows have recovered materially, but the physical market is tight, differentials are strong and shipping costs are elevated. Another 40 million barrels from the SPR gives incremental relief, but depleted inventories mean small imbalances have outsized effects.

Natural gas may be the more important European pressure valve. TTF prices have fallen sharply, and a handful of additional daily Qatari LNG cargoes would materially improve Europe's balance, so confidence in safe passage matters.
On a US-Iran type deal: "Incentives still point to deal but uncertainty is running high and there isn't much time left on the clock."
NY Fed President Williams' "no urgency" comment reduced October hike pricing and modestly steepened the curve. Privorotsky still thinks terminal pricing is aggressive.
Privorotsky says the Fed may ultimately need to hike more, but given how fast financial conditions have tightened it can afford to soften its communication. More Fed speakers are due this week.

AI theme intact: White House message is "accelerate, self-regulate, keep pushing." OpenAI DevDay was evolutionary, and the key development is frontier-level capability getting cheaper and more widely accessible.
Meta bounced sharply as Dots apparently failed to challenge Muse. Robinhood is launching agents that can research, build strategies and trade within user-set limits.

Data was weak on the consumer: confidence fell, inflation expectations rose and job openings softened, which Privorotsky calls "a stagflationary impulse." ADP, GDP and core PCE come next, with PCE "the important one."

Small caps are badly oversold. Privorotsky: "Glass half full a lot of bad news already in the price for everything that isn't AI." Month-end rebalancing could create some duration demand, which could also be a headwind for equities.
Conditions to get more constructive: rates calm, credit stops widening, and a more definitive energy solution. Until then he is not taking nets (net exposure) up.
